The '''Ōshikōchi clan''' ({{lang|ja|凡河内氏}}, ''Ōshikōchi-uji'', also read ''Ōchikawachi-uji'') was an ancient {{ill|Gōzoku|ja|豪族|lt=powerful family|lt_ja=豪族}} whose strength lay mainly in the {{ill|Kinai|ja|畿内|lt=Kinai|lt_ja=畿内}}. The name is also written {{lang|ja|大河内氏}} and Ōshikōchi no {{ill|Imiki|ja|忌寸|lt=Imiki|lt_ja=忌寸}}. See also "{{ill|Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|凡川内国造|lt=Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt_ja=凡川内国造}}" (Kawachi no Kuni no Miyatsuko). One theory reads the words "開中費直" on the {{ill|Suda Hachiman Shrine|ja|隅田八幡宮|lt=Suda Hachiman Shrine|lt_ja=隅田八幡宮}} {{ill|Suda Hachiman Shrine mirror|ja|人物画像鏡|lt=portrait mirror|lt_ja=人物画像鏡}} as "Kawachi no {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}" (かわちのあたい).

There are two lines: one descended from {{ill|Amatsuhikone|ja|天津彦根命|lt=Amatsuhikone|lt_ja=天津彦根命}} (sharing an ancestor with the Nukatabe-no-Yue no Muraji; according to the "{{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|lt=Kokuzō Hongi|lt_ja=国造本紀}}", through his third-generation descendant {{ill|Hikokosohori no Mikoto|ja|彦己曾保理命|lt=Hikokosohori no Mikoto|lt_ja=彦己曾保理命}}), and one that takes as its ancestor {{ill|Umashikarehine no Mikoto|ja|可美乾飯根命|lt=Umashikarehine no Mikoto|lt_ja=可美乾飯根命}}, thirteenth-generation descendant of {{ill|Ame-no-Hohi|ja|天穂日命|lt=Ame-no-Hohi|lt_ja=天穂日命}}.

== Overview ==
The clan held power as the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|lt=kuni no miyatsuko|lt_ja=国造}} family of the ancient {{ill|Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|凡河内国造|lt=Ōshikōchi province|lt_ja=凡河内国}}, a wide area spanning what were later {{ill|Settsu Province|ja|摂津国|lt=Settsu|lt_ja=摂津}}, {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|lt=Kawachi|lt_ja=河内}} and {{ill|Izumi Province|ja|和泉国|lt=Izumi|lt_ja=和泉}}.

=== History ===
The clan first appears in the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi|lt_ja=先代旧事本紀}}'', which says that in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇|lt=Emperor Jimmu|lt_ja=神武天皇}} Hikokosohori no Mikoto (Hikokosone no Mikoto) was appointed {{ill|Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|凡河内国造|lt=Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt_ja=凡河内国造}}.

In the ninth year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|ja|雄略天皇|lt=Emperor Yūryaku|lt_ja=雄略天皇}}, the emperor sent Kagatsu and an {{ill|Uneme|ja|采女|lt=uneme|lt_ja=采女}} (court attendant) to worship the Munakata deity ({{ill|Munakata Sanjojin|ja|宗像三女神|lt=the three Munakata goddesses|lt_ja=宗像三女神}}) and seek an {{ill|Oracle|ja|神託|lt=oracle|lt_ja=神託}} for an expedition against {{ill|Silla|ja|新羅|lt=Silla|lt_ja=新羅}}. But {{ill|Ōshikōchi no Kagatsu|ja|凡河内香賜|lt=Ōshikōchi no Kagatsu|lt_ja=凡河内香賜}}, having reached the sacred ground and being about to perform the {{ill|Shinji|ja|神事|lt=rite|lt_ja=神事}}, lay with the ''uneme''. The emperor, holding this to be sacrilege, sent {{ill|Naniwa no Hitaka|ja|難波日鷹|lt=Naniwa no Kishi Hitaka|lt_ja=難波吉士日鷹}} to kill him, but Kagatsu had fled. The emperor did not give up: he sent {{ill|Yuge no Toyoho|ja|弓削豊穂|lt=Yuge no Muraji Toyoho|lt_ja=弓削連豊穗}}, who had him searched for in every province, district and ''agata'', and at last Kagatsu was caught and beheaded at Aihara in {{ill|Mishima District, Osaka|ja|三島郡 (大阪府)|lt=Mishima District|lt_ja=三島郡}}, near the clan's home ground: later Ai township in {{ill|Shimashimo District|ja|嶋下郡|lt=Shimashimo District|lt_ja=嶋下郡}}, {{ill|Settsu Province|ja|摂津国|lt=Settsu Province|lt_ja=摂津国}} (present-day Ōta, {{ill|Ibaraki, Osaka|ja|茨木市|lt=Ibaraki|lt_ja=茨木市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|lt=Osaka Prefecture|lt_ja=大阪府}}).<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', book 14, Yūryaku 9, second month, first day.</ref>

In the third year of {{ill|Emperor Kenzō|ja|顕宗天皇|lt=Emperor Kenzō|lt_ja=顕宗天皇}}, {{ill|Nakatakōhai|ja|那奇他甲背|lt=Nakatakōhai|lt_ja=那奇他甲背}}, a Wa (Japanese-descended immigrant) living in {{ill|Mimana|ja|任那|lt=Mimana|lt_ja=任那}}, supported {{ill|Ki no Ōiwa|ja|紀大磐|lt=Ki no Ōiwa no Sukune|lt_ja=紀生磐宿禰}} in his attempt to become king of the three Han, failed, and is said to have been killed by {{ill|Baekje|ja|百済|lt=Baekje|lt_ja=百済}}.<ref>''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|lt=Nihon Shoki|lt_ja=日本書紀}}'', Kenzō 3.</ref>

In the seventh month of the third year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|ja|欽明天皇|lt=Emperor Kinmei|lt_ja=欽明天皇}}, King {{ill|Seong of Baekje|ja|聖明王|lt=Seong|lt_ja=聖明王}} tried to restore Mimana, which {{ill|Silla|ja|新羅|lt=Silla|lt_ja=新羅}} had invaded. The officials of the {{ill|Mimana Nihon-fu|ja|任那日本府|lt=Mimana Nihon-fu|lt_ja=任那日本府}} at {{ill|Ara (Gaya)|ja|安羅|lt=Ara|lt_ja=安羅}}, {{ill|Kawachi no Atai|ja|河内直|lt=Kawachi no Atai|lt_ja=河内直}}, {{ill|Ienashi|ja|移那斯|lt=Ienashi|lt_ja=移那斯}} and {{ill|Matsu (Mimana official)|ja|麻都|lt=Matsu|lt_ja=麻都}} (in the "Kudara Hongi", Kafushichi no Atai, Akeenashi and Saromatsu), were in league with Silla and were rebuked by Seong.<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', Kinmei 3, seventh month.</ref> {{ill|Kimiaki Mori|ja|森公章|lt=Mori Kimiaki|lt_ja=森公章}} and {{ill|Kōsaku Hamada|ja|濱田耕策|lt=Hamada Kōsaku|lt_ja=濱田耕策}} take Nakatakōhai of Mimana as the ancestor and {{ill|Karyōjikikōhai|ja|加猟直岐甲背|lt=Karyōjikikōhai|lt_ja=加猟直岐甲背}} Yōkikimi{{efn|Mori Kimiaki and Hamada Kōsaku suppose that Karyōjikikōhai and Yōkikimi are the same person.}} as his son, and conclude that Kawachi no Atai was born to Karyōjikikōhai and a Wa wife, and Ienashi and Matsu to him and a Baekje or {{ill|Gaya confederacy|ja|伽耶|lt=Kara|lt_ja=加羅}} wife.<ref>{{Cite news|author={{ill|Kimiaki Mori|ja|森公章|lt=Mori Kimiaki|lt_ja=森公章}} and {{ill|Kōsaku Hamada|ja|濱田耕策|lt=Hamada Kōsaku|lt_ja=浜田耕策}}|date=2010|title=古代王権の成長と日韓関係 ―4~6世紀―|trans-title=The growth of ancient royal power and Japan–Korea relations, 4th–6th centuries|publisher={{ill|Japan-Korea Joint History Research|ja|日韓歴史共同研究|lt=Japan–Korea Joint History Research|lt_ja=日韓歴史共同研究}}|newspaper=日韓歴史共同研究報告書（第2期）|url=https://www.jkcf.or.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2010/10/1-allj.pdf|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813102055/https://www.jkcf.or.jp/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2010/10/1-allj.pdf|format=PDF|archivedate=2022-08-13|page=144}}</ref> In the fifth month of Kinmei 13, {{ill|Kawachibe no Ashihita|ja|河内部阿斯比多|lt=Kawachibe no Ashihita|lt_ja=河内部阿斯比多}} was sent from Baekje, Kara and Ara, and returned to Baekje on the 13th day of the first month of the following year.<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', Kinmei 13, fifth month.</ref><ref>''Nihon Shoki'', Kinmei 14, first month.</ref>

According to book 29 of the ''Nihon Shoki'', in {{ill|681|ja|681年|lt=681|lt_ja=681年}} (the fourth month of the tenth year of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|lt=Emperor Tenmu|lt_ja=天武天皇}}), Kawachi no Atai Agata was granted the {{ill|Kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} {{ill|Muraji|ja|連|lt=muraji|lt_ja=連}}.<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', Tenmu 10, fourth month, twelfth day.</ref>

Because the clan had one of its bases at Aihara in {{ill|Mishima District, Osaka|ja|三島郡 (大阪府)|lt=Mishima District|lt_ja=三島郡}}, and because {{ill|Ōshikōchi no Wakugohime|ja|大河内稚子媛|lt=Ōshikōchi no Wakugohime|lt_ja=大河内稚子媛}}, daughter of {{ill|Ōshikōchi no Ajihari|ja|大河内味張|lt=Ōshikōchi no Atai Ajihari|lt_ja=大河内直味張}}, appears as a {{ill|Hi (consort)|ja|妃|lt=consort|lt_ja=妃}} of {{ill|Emperor Senka|ja|宣化天皇|lt=Emperor Senka|lt_ja=宣化天皇}}, one theory supposes a close relationship with the family of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇|lt=Emperor Keitai|lt_ja=継体天皇}}, who lived in Mishima. The same theory holds that the {{ill|Takafu Miyake|ja|竹村屯倉|lt=Takafu miyake|lt_ja=竹村屯倉}} was cultivated by {{ill|Tabe|ja|田部|lt=tabe|lt_ja=田部}} of Kawachi sent by the Ōshikōchi (Ajihari and others), and takes this to mean that the clan managed the farming of the Keitai family's lands.<ref>{{Cite book|author={{ill|Miyaji Kakuno|ja|客野宮治|lt=Kakuno Miyaji|lt_ja=客野宮治}}|date=2015-04-01|title=蘇我氏の研究|trans-title=Studies of the Soga clan|publisher={{ill|Bungeisha|ja|文芸社|lt=Bungeisha|lt_ja=文芸社}}|ISBN=4286160939}}</ref>

The ''{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|lt=Shoku Nihongi|lt_ja=続日本紀}}'' records that in the tenth month of {{ill|Keiun|ja|慶雲|lt=Keiun|lt_ja=慶雲}} 3 ({{ill|706|ja|706年|lt=706|lt_ja=706年}}) the Settsu ''kuni no miyatsuko'' {{ill|Ōshikōchi no Iwamaro|ja|凡河内石麻呂|lt=Ōshikōchi no Imiki Iwamaro|lt_ja=凡河内忌寸石麻呂}} was raised one step from {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank|ja|従七位|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Upper Grade|lt_ja=従七位上}}, so the clan also supplied the ''kuni no miyatsuko'' of Settsu. By the {{ill|Nara period|ja|奈良時代|lt=Nara period|lt_ja=奈良時代}}, however, its former power is thought to have declined.

In {{ill|Ubara District|ja|菟原郡|lt=Ubara District|lt_ja=菟原郡}}, Settsu, stands {{ill|Kawachi Kunitama Shrine|ja|河内国魂神社|lt=Kawachi Kunitama Shrine|lt_ja=河内国魂神社}} (Gomō Tenjin), thought to have been served by the Ōshikōchi clan. The ''{{ill|Hōryū-ji Garan Engi narabi ni Ruki Shizaichō|ja|法隆寺伽藍縁起并流記資財帖|lt=Hōryū-ji Garan Engi narabi ni Ruki Shizaichō|lt_ja=法隆寺伽藍縁起并流記資財帖}}'' of {{ill|Tenpyō|ja|天平|lt=Tenpyō|lt_ja=天平}} 19 ({{ill|747|ja|747年|lt=747|lt_ja=747年}}) names {{ill|Ōshikōchi-dera Mountain|ja|凡河内寺山|lt=Ōshikōchi-dera Mountain|lt_ja=凡河内寺山}} near {{ill|Mount Ege|ja|会下山|lt=Mount Ege|lt_ja=会下山}} in Settsu.

According to the ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|lt=Shoku Nihon Kōki|lt_ja=続日本後紀}}'', in the second month of Tenchō 10 ({{ill|833|ja|833年|lt=833|lt_ja=833年}}) three men of Settsu, Ōshikōchi no Imiki Kinunushi (unassigned, Junior Sixth Rank Upper), his elder brother Kimaro (Junior Eighth Rank Upper) and his younger brother Fukunaga (Greater Initial Rank Lower), were granted the name Kiyōchi no Sukune.

In the early {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|lt=Heian period|lt_ja=平安時代}} the clan produced the {{ill|Waka|ja|歌人|lt=poet|lt_ja=歌人}} {{ill|Ōshikōchi no Mitsune|ja|凡河内躬恒|lt=Ōshikōchi no Mitsune|lt_ja=凡河内躬恒}}.
